audit_status.source_base: Greek Romans text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Israel not rejected, remnant, jealousy, olive tree warning, mystery, all Israel, mercy on all, doxology. Strong anti-replacement safeguards required.

verses.restored: I say then, did the Divine reject his people? May it not be. For I also am an Israelite, from seed of Abraham, tribe of Benjamin.

familiar.text: I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

modern.text: I ask then, did God reject His people? Certainly not! I am an Israelite myself, a descendant of Abraham, from the tribe of Benjamin.

original.text: Λέγω οὖν, μὴ ἀπώσατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ; μὴ γένοιτο· καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ Ἰσραηλίτης εἰμί, ἐκ σπέρματος Ἀβραάμ, φυλῆς Βενιαμίν.

verses.restored: The Divine did not reject his people whom he foreknew. Or do you not know what the Scripture says in Elijah, how he appeals to the Divine against Israel?

familiar.text: God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew. Wot ye not what the scripture saith of Elias? how he maketh intercession to God against Israel, saying,

modern.text: God did not reject His people, whom He foreknew. Do you not know what the Scripture says about Elijah, how he appealed to God against Israel:

original.text: οὐκ ἀπώσατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ὃν προέγνω. ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ἐν Ἠλίᾳ τί λέγει ἡ γραφή, ὡς ἐντυγχάνει τῷ θεῷ κατὰ τοῦ ⸀Ἰσραήλ;

verses.restored: Lord, they killed your prophets; they tore down your altars; I alone was left, and they seek my life.

familiar.text: Lord, they have killed thy prophets, and digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life.

modern.text: “Lord, they have killed Your prophets and torn down Your altars. I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well” ?

original.text: Κύριε, τοὺς προφήτας σου ἀπέκτειναν, ⸀τὰ θυσιαστήριά σου κατέσκαψαν, κἀγὼ ὑπελείφθην μόνος, καὶ ζητοῦσιν τὴν ψυχήν μου.

verses.restored: But what does the divine answer say to him? I left for myself seven thousand men who did not bend knee to Baal.

familiar.text: But what saith the answer of God unto him? I have reserved to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal.

modern.text: And what was the divine reply to him? “I have reserved for Myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.”

original.text: ἀλλὰ τί λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ χρηματισμός; Κατέλιπον ἐμαυτῷ ἑπτακισχιλίους ἄνδρας, οἵτινες οὐκ ἔκαμψαν γόνυ τῇ Βάαλ.

verses.restored: So then also in the present time there has come to be a remnant according to choosing of grace.

familiar.text: Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.

modern.text: In the same way, at the present time there is a remnant chosen by grace.

original.text: οὕτως οὖν καὶ ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ λεῖμμα κατʼ ἐκλογὴν χάριτος γέγονεν·

verses.restored: But if by grace, no longer from works; otherwise grace no longer becomes grace.

familiar.text: And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then is it no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.

modern.text: And if it is by grace, then it is no longer by works. Otherwise, grace would no longer be grace.

original.text: εἰ δὲ χάριτι, οὐκέτι ἐξ ἔργων, ἐπεὶ ἡ χάρις οὐκέτι γίνεται ⸀χάρις.

verses.restored: What then? What Israel seeks, this it did not obtain, but the chosen obtained; the rest were hardened,

familiar.text: What then? Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for; but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded.

modern.text: What then? What Israel was seeking, it failed to obtain, but the elect did. The others were hardened,

original.text: τί οὖν; ὃ ἐπιζητεῖ Ἰσραήλ, τοῦτο οὐκ ἐπέτυχεν, ἡ δὲ ἐκλογὴ ἐπέτυχεν· οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ ἐπωρώθησαν,

verses.restored: just as it is written: The Divine gave them a spirit of deep sleep, eyes not to see and ears not to hear, until this day.

familiar.text: (According as it is written, God hath given them the spirit of slumber, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear;) unto this day.

modern.text: as it is written: “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that could not see, and ears that could not hear, to this very day.”

original.text: ⸀καθὼς γέγραπται· Ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς πνεῦμα κατανύξεως, ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ μὴ βλέπειν καὶ ὦτα τοῦ μὴ ἀκούειν, ἕως τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας.

verses.restored: And David says: Let their table become a snare and a trap and a stumbling block and a repayment to them;

familiar.text: And David saith, Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumblingblock, and a recompence unto them:

modern.text: And David says: “May their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a retribution to them.

original.text: καὶ Δαυὶδ λέγει· Γενηθήτω ἡ τράπεζα αὐτῶν εἰς παγίδα καὶ εἰς θήραν καὶ εἰς σκάνδαλον καὶ εἰς ἀνταπόδομα αὐτοῖς,

verses.restored: let their eyes be darkened not to see, and bend their back through all.

familiar.text: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back alway.

modern.text: May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever.” The Ingrafting of the Gentiles

original.text: σκοτισθήτωσαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν τοῦ μὴ βλέπειν, καὶ τὸν νῶτον αὐτῶν διὰ παντὸς σύγκαμψον.

verses.restored: I say then, did they stumble so that they might fall? May it not be. But by their trespass salvation/healing has come to the nations, to provoke them to jealousy.

familiar.text: I say then, Have they stumbled that they should fall? God forbid: but rather through their fall salvation is come unto the Gentiles, for to provoke them to jealousy.

modern.text: I ask then, did they stumble so as to fall beyond recovery? Certainly not! However, because of their trespass, salvation has come to the Gentiles to make Israel jealous.

original.text: Λέγω οὖν, μὴ ἔπταισαν ἵνα πέσωσιν; μὴ γένοιτο· ἀλλὰ τῷ αὐτῶν παραπτώματι ἡ σωτηρία τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, εἰς τὸ παραζηλῶσαι αὐτούς.

verses.restored: Now if their trespass is riches of world, and their loss riches of nations, how much more their fullness?

familiar.text: Now if the fall of them be the riches of the world, and the diminishing of them the riches of the Gentiles; how much more their fulness?

modern.text: But if their trespass means riches for the world, and their failure means riches for the Gentiles, how much greater riches will their fullness bring!

original.text: εἰ δὲ τὸ παράπτωμα αὐτῶν πλοῦτος κόσμου καὶ τὸ ἥττημα αὐτῶν πλοῦτος ἐθνῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: But I speak to you, the nations. Inasmuch then as I am apostle of nations, I glorify my service,

familiar.text: For I speak to you Gentiles, inasmuch as I am the apostle of the Gentiles, I magnify mine office:

modern.text: I am speaking to you Gentiles. Inasmuch as I am the apostle to the Gentiles, I magnify my ministry

original.text: Ὑμῖν ⸀δὲ λέγω τοῖς ἔθνεσιν. ἐφʼ ὅσον μὲν ⸀οὖν εἰμι ἐγὼ ἐθνῶν ἀπόστολος, τὴν διακονίαν μου δοξάζω,

verses.restored: if somehow I might provoke my flesh to jealousy and save/heal some of them.

familiar.text: If by any means I may provoke to emulation them which are my flesh, and might save some of them.

modern.text: in the hope that I may provoke my own people to jealousy and save some of them.

original.text: εἴ πως παραζηλώσω μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ σώσω τινὰς ἐξ αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: For if their rejection is reconciliation of world, what will their acceptance be if not life from the dead?

familiar.text: For if the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world, what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead?

modern.text: For if their rejection is the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance be but life from the dead?

original.text: εἰ γὰρ ἡ ἀποβολὴ αὐτῶν καταλλαγὴ κόσμου, τίς ἡ πρόσλημψις εἰ μὴ ζωὴ ἐκ νεκρῶν;

verses.restored: If the firstfruit is holy, also the lump; and if the root is holy, also the branches.

familiar.text: For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches.

modern.text: If the first part of the dough is holy, so is the whole batch; if the root is holy, so are the branches.

original.text: εἰ δὲ ἡ ἀπαρχὴ ἁγία, καὶ τὸ φύραμα· καὶ εἰ ἡ ῥίζα ἁγία, καὶ οἱ κλάδοι.

verses.restored: But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being wild olive, were grafted in among them and became sharer of the rich root of the olive tree,

familiar.text: And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree;

modern.text: Now if some branches have been broken off, and you, a wild olive shoot, have been grafted in among the others to share in the nourishment of the olive root,

original.text: Εἰ δέ τινες τῶν κλάδων ἐξεκλάσθησαν, σὺ δὲ ἀγριέλαιος ὢν ἐνεκεντρίσθης ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ συγκοινωνὸς τῆς ⸀ῥίζης τῆς πιότητος τῆς ἐλαίας ἐγένου,

verses.restored: do not boast over the branches. But if you boast, remember: you do not support the root, but the root supports you.

familiar.text: Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee.

modern.text: do not boast over those branches. If you do, remember this: You do not support the root, but the root supports you.

original.text: μὴ κατακαυχῶ τῶν κλάδων· εἰ δὲ κατακαυχᾶσαι, οὐ σὺ τὴν ῥίζαν βαστάζεις ἀλλὰ ἡ ῥίζα σέ.

verses.restored: You will say then, Branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in.

familiar.text: Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be graffed in.

modern.text: You will say then, “Branches were broken off so that I could be grafted in.”

original.text: ἐρεῖς οὖν· Ἐξεκλάσθησαν κλάδοι ἵνα ἐγὼ ἐγκεντρισθῶ.

verses.restored: Beautifully/well; by untrust they were broken off, but you stand by trust. Do not be high-minded, but fear/revere.

familiar.text: Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear:

modern.text: That is correct: They were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand by faith. Do not be arrogant, but be afraid.

original.text: καλῶς· τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἐξεκλάσθησαν, σὺ δὲ τῇ πίστει ἕστηκας. μὴ ⸂ὑψηλὰ φρόνει⸃, ἀλλὰ φοβοῦ·

verses.restored: For if the Divine did not spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you.

familiar.text: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.

modern.text: For if God did not spare the natural branches, He will certainly not spare you either.

original.text: εἰ γὰρ ὁ θεὸς τῶν κατὰ φύσιν κλάδων οὐκ ἐφείσατο, ⸀οὐδὲ σοῦ φείσεται.

verses.restored: See therefore kindness and severity of the Divine: upon those who fell, severity; but upon you, kindness of the Divine, if you remain in kindness; otherwise you also will be cut off.

familiar.text: Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off.

modern.text: Take notice, therefore, of the kindness and severity of God: severity to those who fell, but kindness to you, if you continue in His kindness. Otherwise you also will be cut off.

original.text: ἴδε οὖν χρηστότητα καὶ ἀποτομίαν θεοῦ· ἐπὶ μὲν τοὺς πεσόντας ⸀ἀποτομία, ἐπὶ δὲ σὲ ⸂χρηστότης θεοῦ⸃, ἐὰν ⸀ἐπιμένῃς τῇ χρηστότητι, ἐπεὶ καὶ σὺ ἐκκοπήσῃ.

verses.restored: And those also, if they do not remain in untrust, will be grafted in; for the Divine is powerful to graft them in again.

familiar.text: And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief, shall be graffed in: for God is able to graff them in again.

modern.text: And if they do not persist in unbelief, they will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.

original.text: κἀκεῖνοι δέ, ἐὰν μὴ ⸀ἐπιμένωσι τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ, ἐγκεντρισθήσονται· δυνατὸς γάρ ⸂ἐστιν ὁ θεὸς⸃ πάλιν ἐγκεντρίσαι αὐτούς.

verses.restored: For if you were cut from what is by nature a wild olive tree and against nature were grafted into cultivated olive, how much more will these natural ones be grafted into their own olive tree?

familiar.text: For if thou wert cut out of the olive tree which is wild by nature, and wert graffed contrary to nature into a good olive tree: how much more shall these, which be the natural branches, be graffed into their own olive tree?

modern.text: For if you were cut from a wild olive tree, and contrary to nature were grafted into one that is cultivated, how much more readily will these, the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree! All Israel Will Be Saved

original.text: εἰ γὰρ σὺ ἐκ τῆς κατὰ φύσιν ἐξεκόπης ἀγριελαίου καὶ παρὰ φύσιν ἐνεκεντρίσθης εἰς καλλιέλαιον, πόσῳ μᾶλλον οὗτοι οἱ κατὰ φύσιν ἐγκεντρισθήσονται τῇ ἰδίᾳ ἐλαίᾳ.

verses.restored: For I do not want you to be unaware, siblings, of this mystery, so that you may not be wise in yourselves: a hardening in part has happened to Israel until the fullness of the nations comes in,

familiar.text: For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.

modern.text: I do not want you to be ignorant of this mystery, brothers, so that you will not be conceited: A hardening in part has come to Israel, until the full number of the Gentiles has come in.

original.text: Οὐ γὰρ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, τὸ μυστήριον τοῦτο, ἵνα μὴ ⸀ἦτε ἑαυτοῖς φρόνιμοι, ὅτι πώρωσις ἀπὸ μέρους τῷ Ἰσραὴλ γέγονεν ἄχρι οὗ τὸ πλήρωμα τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰσέλθῃ,

verses.restored: and so all Israel will be saved/healed, just as it is written: The Deliverer will come from Zion; he will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.

familiar.text: And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob:

modern.text: And so all Israel will be saved, as it is written: “The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will remove godlessness from Jacob.

original.text: καὶ οὕτως πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ σωθήσεται· καθὼς γέγραπται· Ἥξει ἐκ Σιὼν ὁ ⸀ῥυόμενος, ἀποστρέψει ἀσεβείας ἀπὸ Ἰακώβ.

verses.restored: And this is the covenant from me to them, when I take away their sins/misalignments.

familiar.text: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.

modern.text: And this is My covenant with them when I take away their sins.”

original.text: καὶ αὕτη αὐτοῖς ἡ παρʼ ἐμοῦ διαθήκη, ὅταν ἀφέλωμαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: According to the good news, they are opposed for your sake; but according to choosing, beloved because of the fathers.

familiar.text: As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the fathers’ sakes.

modern.text: Regarding the gospel, they are enemies on your account; but regarding election, they are loved on account of the patriarchs.

original.text: κατὰ μὲν τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ἐχθροὶ διʼ ὑμᾶς, κατὰ δὲ τὴν ἐκλογὴν ἀγαπητοὶ διὰ τοὺς πατέρας·

verses.restored: For the gifts and the calling of the Divine are irrevocable.

familiar.text: For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance.

modern.text: For God’s gifts and His call are irrevocable.

original.text: ἀμεταμέλητα γὰρ τὰ χαρίσματα καὶ ἡ κλῆσις τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: For just as you once disobeyed the Divine, but now were shown mercy by their disobedience,

familiar.text: For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief:

modern.text: Just as you who formerly disobeyed God have now received mercy through their disobedience,

original.text: ὥσπερ ⸀γὰρ ὑμεῖς ποτε ἠπειθήσατε τῷ θεῷ, νῦν δὲ ἠλεήθητε τῇ τούτων ἀπειθείᾳ,

verses.restored: so also these now disobeyed by the mercy shown to you, so that they also now may be shown mercy.

familiar.text: Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy.

modern.text: so they too have now disobeyed, in order that they too may now receive mercy through the mercy shown to you.

original.text: οὕτως καὶ οὗτοι νῦν ἠπείθησαν τῷ ὑμετέρῳ ἐλέει ἵνα καὶ αὐτοὶ ⸀νῦν ἐλεηθῶσιν·

verses.restored: For the Divine enclosed all into disobedience, so that he might show mercy to all.

familiar.text: For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all.

modern.text: For God has consigned everyone to disobedience so that He may have mercy on everyone. A Hymn of Praise (Isaiah 40:9–31)

original.text: συνέκλεισεν γὰρ ὁ θεὸς τοὺς πάντας εἰς ἀπείθειαν ἵνα τοὺς πάντας ἐλεήσῃ.

verses.restored: O depth of riches and wisdom and knowledge of the Divine. How unsearchable his judgments and untraceable his ways.

familiar.text: O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!

modern.text: O, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments, and untraceable His ways!

original.text: Ὦ βάθος πλούτου καὶ σοφίας καὶ γνώσεως θεοῦ· ὡς ἀνεξεραύνητα τὰ κρίματα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀνεξιχνίαστοι αἱ ὁδοὶ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: For who knew the mind of the Lord? Or who became his counselor?

familiar.text: For who hath known the mind of the Lord? or who hath been his counsellor?

modern.text: “Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been His counselor?”

original.text: Τίς γὰρ ἔγνω νοῦν κυρίου; ἢ τίς σύμβουλος αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο;

verses.restored: Or who first gave to him, and it will be repaid to him?

familiar.text: Or who hath first given to him, and it shall be recompensed unto him again?

modern.text: “Who has first given to God, that God should repay him?”

original.text: ἢ τίς προέδωκεν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἀνταποδοθήσεται αὐτῷ;

verses.restored: Because from him and through him and into him are all things. To him be glory into the ages. Amen.

familiar.text: For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things: to whom be glory for ever. Amen.

modern.text: For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory forever! Amen.

original.text: ὅτι ἐξ αὐτοῦ καὶ διʼ αὐτοῦ καὶ εἰς αὐτὸν τὰ πάντα· αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, ἀμήν.

safety_note: Romans 11 explicitly rejects the idea that the Divine rejected Israel. It warns nations-believers not to boast over Israel and grounds the argument in irrevocable gifts/calling and mercy on all. This chapter is a major anti-replacement anchor.
